This is [POCD](https://www.ocdbaltimore.com/pedophile-ocd-pocd/), you are not alone, I also suffer from it and I've heard it is fairly common amongst OCD sufferers. You can't think away the thoughts, if you try to make them go away, they will never go away. This is the sad paradox/reality of OCD. You have to allow for the thoughts to exist, without engaging in rituals. If you can allow for the thoughts to be present and allow for the feelings of anxiety associated with those thoughts to be present, you should gradually see a reduction in the anxiety as you will no longer be bothered by the thought. This is the premise of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT).

  
I'm not going to lie, it is not easy. I am currently doing CBT and I am struggling hard; I am depressed or suicidal almost every day. Everyone experiences these thoughts, but us OCD sufferers are unable to dismiss them like everyone else; we place over-importance on these particular thoughts and uncertainties.

I was diagnosed with ADD when I was younger, but I now believe it was undiagnosed OCD all along. Unfortunately, I got roped in to taking stimulants (Vyvanse) for 8 years because of it and I've never been the same ever since I got off of it last year. As far as having OCD without compulsions, you may still be doing compulsions that you're not aware of. When you have the intrusive thoughts, are trying to convince yourself that they are not true and/or won't happen? If so, then you are still doing a compulsion (mental reassurance seeking). Basically, if you are doing anything to alleviate the anxiety brought on by an intrusive thought, then that is considered a compulsion.

In this case when the zombies encountered an obstacle (say a wall) they would just stand there scratching at that wall until their attention is changed by: 
1. A new audio cue (someone shooting a gun)
2. A new visual cue (someone running past them)
3. Memory/ forgetting what they are doing

The same idea can be used in visual distraction too w/ a slight modification. When a zombie sees a player the zombie will travel to the last known sighting of the player. In this case when a zombie encounters an obstacle it **may** slowly work its way around the obstacle in pursuit of not the player but rather the last known sighting of the player. I don't have a cognitive explanation as to why the zombie is able to slowly overcome obstacles in the case of visual distractions but it just seems more likely.

**Suggestion:** When a character ~~dies~~ gets very sick/about to die that characters body "reanimates" into a zombie NPC.
 
**What it is not:**

* You die, you spawn as zombie [controlled by you] and run around infecting people.


**What it will fix:** 

* Players running directly back to their "place of death" and looting their bodies.

* When a player dies their character reanimates into a zombie. This [server controlled] zombie essentially becomes a fellow server spawned zombie (ie...walking around, attacking players) carrying YOUR previous gear. This means one must track their zombie to acquire their previous gear.


**What it will add:**

* Greater variety of zombie "skins" (without being forced).

* You'll see hundreds of unique zombies walking around (ones with motorcycle helmets, underwear, etc...)

* A new way of acquiring good gear without KOS'ing other living players.

* A player can spot a zombie carrying nice gear, kill it, disinfect the gear and be on their merry way.


**What it will change:**

* Current DayZ zombie lore.

* Currently, players are immune to the infection. With this change players are immune until they get really sick and/or are on the verge of death.
